summary: Verify front direction, mount, size and city use of every Decimation prop/decal, two independent readers per family plus judge

merged.name: BlockStreetLight
merged.looks_like: tall dark lamp post (6 block pole) with one curved arm and lamp head reaching about 2.6 blocks sideways at the top
merged.meta_range_note: 2..5 (PropRenderer uses meta%4*90, so 0 acts as 4 and 1 as 5); placer writes 2..5 only
real_world_city_use: main street lighting on both sidewalks, head hanging over the outer lane
apocalypse: many bent or missing, still the dominant skyline element of a street
placement_rules: stand on the sidewalk cell touching the curb, arm pointing over the road: road to the east meta 2, south 3, west 4, north 5
spacing about 16 to 24 blocks along a side, the two sides staggered by half a spacing (current LegacyStreets: every 20, staggered 10, 25% missing)
keep 8 cells above the post free and the 2 to 3 cells under the arm free above head height (no trees, awnings, other lamp heads)
never in an intersection corner cell (traffic lights go there) and not in front of a door
merged.evidence: PropBlockRegistry line 522 (bmodel streetlight, extra rotation 180); dirs via tools/props/propgeom.py matrices: model +x -> m2 E, m3 S; bmodel parts: arm baseModel3..7 toward +x; prop_geometry.tsv meta 2 x 0.41..3.07; in game confirmed meta 2 arm east (docs/shots_index.md street_v0.15 autotest_1); gallery_51 shows the pole
merged.tile_entity_cost: cheap (8 bmodel parts, PropRenderer with line of sight culling)
rules_second: stand on the sidewalk cell right next to the curb, arm pointing over the road: road east m2, road south m3, road west m4, road north m5
spacing 16 to 24 blocks along a side, both sides staggered by half that
keep 7 cells above free, and keep the arm path clear (y+6..y+8, 3 cells toward the road): no awnings, trees or overhangs
never in the middle of the walkway or in front of a door
use_second: sidewalk street lighting on every street; in a dead city many are unlit or leaning, but they still line the curb
parking lots, plazas, bridge decks

merged.front_feature: none, two arms opposite each other along model x
merged.meta_range_note: 2..5; 2 and 4 are the same look (arms E and W), 3 and 5 the same (arms N and S)
real_world_city_use: central median of a wide boulevard or divided highway lighting both carriageways
parking lots, plazas, bridge decks
placement_rules: on a median or island cell, arms ACROSS the road: north-south street meta 2 or 4, east-west street meta 3 or 5
needs about 2.5 free cells on both sides at the top (arms span x -2.2..3.1 at meta 2), 8 cells free above
spacing like single lamps (16 to 24 blocks); do not use on narrow 2 lane streets without a median
merged.evidence: PropBlockRegistry line 524 (extra 180); bmodel streetlightmiddle parts baseModel3..7 (+x arm) and 8..13 (-x arm); prop_geometry.tsv meta 2 x -2.18..3.07, meta 3 z -2.18..3.07
rules_second: only in a median with road on both sides; arms across the road: N-S road needs arms E-W (meta 2/4), E-W road needs arms N-S (meta 3/5)
spacing 16 to 24 along the median
7 free cells above and 3 cells clear on both sides at y+6..y+8
use_second: central median or traffic island of a divided avenue or boulevard
middle of a wide parking lot

merged.name: BlockTrafficLights
merged.looks_like: tall signal pole with a mast arm 6.9 blocks long carrying two hanging 3 lamp signal heads, small street lamp on top
merged.front_feature: signal lenses (visors on model +z); the arm runs along model +x
merged.meta_range_note: 2..5; arm points 2 E, 3 S, 4 W, 5 N; the lenses face 90 degrees to the LEFT of the arm direction
real_world_city_use: US mast arm signal at the far right corner of an intersection, arm over the approach lanes, lenses toward approaching drivers
apocalypse: dark, still standing at every major crossing
placement_rules: one per approach, on the sidewalk corner cell at the FAR RIGHT side of the intersection for that approach
northbound traffic (lenses S): pole at the NE corner, meta 4 (arm W over the road)
southbound (lenses N): pole at the SW corner, meta 2 (arm E)
eastbound (lenses W): pole at the SE corner, meta 5 (arm N)
westbound (lenses E): pole at the NW corner, meta 3 (arm S)
arm is 7 long: keep 8 cells above the pole and the cells under the arm (height 4.3..6) free; heads hang 1.9 and 5.2 blocks from the pole
no street lamp within 3 blocks of the pole (it already has a lamp on top)
merged.evidence: PropBlockRegistry line 526 (bmodel trafficlight, extra 180); bmodel parts: pole baseModel0, arm baseModel2 x 1..111, heads baseModel10 and 35 (back plate z 0..1) with visors baseModel11..34 at z 1..4 => lenses model +z; propgeom matrices: +z -> m2 N, m3 E, m4 S, m5 W, +x -> m2 E, m3 S; prop_geometry.tsv meta 3 z 0.41..7.44; gallery_54 (heads visible, too small to read lenses)
rules_second: pole on the sidewalk corner that is the FAR RIGHT corner of the approach it controls (right hand traffic), arm out over that approach's lanes, lenses facing the approaching drivers

westbound approach: meta 3 at the NW corner (arm S, lenses E); eastbound: meta 5 at the SE corner (arm N, lenses W); southbound: meta 2 at the SW corner (arm E, lenses N); northbound: meta 4 at the NE corner (arm W, lenses S)
up to 4 per crossing, one per approach; road at least 6 wide so heads hang over lanes
7 cells above free and the arm corridor (y+4..y+8, 7 cells long) clear of buildings
use_second: signalised intersections of the main grid, one pole per approach
dead city: still standing, dark; some approaches missing

arms span 7 blocks across the road (x -2.9..3.9 at meta 2): road plus median must be at least 7 wide or the arm overhangs the sidewalk
6 cells above free, nothing under the arms above 4 blocks

lenses toward the approaching traffic: westbound m3, eastbound m5, southbound m2, northbound m4
heads hang 1.5 and 2.4 out: only for roads at least 3 wide on each side
6 cells above free, arms clear at y+4..y+6
use_second: median or pedestrian island at a signalised crossing of a divided road
stop line of a one-way avenue

real_world_city_use: Walls beside bodies (SkeletonWall, SkeletonGround, body bags), hospital and clinic corridors, behind barricades where a fight happened, apartment rooms where someone turned, police station cells
placement_rules: Wall only: the quad is always upright, so there is no floor or ceiling blood. The cell must be air with a full solid block face on the cling side (m2 W, m3 N, m4 E, m5 S); the splatter looks away from it (wall north gives 3, south 5, west 2, east 4)

Drawn 2x2 centred on the cell, 0.02 off the wall (meta 3: x -0.5..1.5, y -0.5..1.5). The wall face must be solid for the side neighbours and for the rows below and above too. Not across door gaps, windows, panes or corners

At walking level the lower half hides in the floor and the blood seems to run up from the floor (about 0..1.4 visible). At walking level +1 it reads as a hit at body height (0.56..2.38). Both are good
Cluster 1 or 2 splats around a body scene; centres at least 2 apart; mix splat 1..5 so no two neighbours are equal
No other wall prop within one cell sideways or up and down; it would overlap
merged.evidence: deobf/src/decimation/block/DecalBlockRegistry.java: bloodsplat1 setDecalSize(2). decimation/block/BlockDecal.java: onBlockPlacedBy yaw to 5/2/3/4, bounds 2..5, no collision boxes. decimation/render/DecalRenderer.java: T(+1,+1,+1), Rx 180, then per meta%4: 3 gives Ry 0 and T(-1,0,0.98), so the quad sits at z 0.02 (north face); 2 gives Ry 270 and T(-0.98,0,0), quad at x 0.02 (west face); 0 (=4) gives Ry 90 and T(-0.01,0,1), quad at x 0.99 (east face); 1 (=5) gives Ry 180, quad at z 1.0 (south face). RenderUtil.e/c draw the quad centred at (0.5,0.5), size decalSize. The CCW winding gives a front normal of -z local, which is south in the world at meta 3. Tiny coordinate based offset against z fighting. Texture assets/deci/textures/blocks/decal/bloodsplat1.png 32x32. docs/shots/gallery_v0.16/gallery_76.png (meta 3, visible from the south)
merged.tile_entity_cost: cheap: one textured quad TESR, StaticTileEntity (no tick)
rules_second: 1. Block goes in the AIR cell against a solid wall; meta = picture away from the wall: wall N use 3, wall S use 5, wall W use 2, wall E use 4. The quad hugs that wall face (0.01 to 0.02 off it).
2. Never on glass, doors, fences or open air: the plane sits on the cell edge, so without a full block behind it floats.
3. One decal per wall cell; do not overlap graffiti, the wall flag or a keycard screen.
4. Size 2: the splat is 2 x 2 centred on the cell and reaches 0.5 into the wall cells left, right, above and below; those must be wall too (not glass or door).
5. Height: Y0+1 puts the centre 1.5 above the floor (shot / bite height, the realistic spot). At Y0 the lower half is hidden inside the floor block (low smear).

6. Group 1 to 3 with a story (skeletons, body bags, hanging body, broken barricade, police / hospital rooms, apartment corridors); 2 cells between splats on one wall; a few per city block, not on every building.
use_second: Interior walls of fight scenes: corridors, hospital rooms, police cells, bathrooms; exterior walls behind car wrecks

judged.evidence:
The renderer is deobf/src/decimation/render/RoadsignParkingRenderer.java. It translates by +0.5, 0, +0.5, runs glRotatef(180, 0.1, 0, 0) (180 about x) and then glRotatef(n, 0, 1, 0) with meta%4 giving 0:180, 1:270, 2:0, 3:90. It binds textures/model/blocks/props/roadsign_parking.png (64x128, 2x the model's 32x64).

ModelRoadsign (deobf/src/decimation/model/ModelRoadsign.java) has two parts. nx is the pole: box 1x33x1 at (-0.5, -33, -0.5). ny is the plate: addBox(0,0,0,1,10,9) at (0, -35, -4.5), texture offset (9,1). The plate is thin along model x and sits at model x 0..1, the +x side of the pole.

Key point: `ny.mirror = true` is set AFTER `addBox`. ModelBox reads mirror inside the constructor, so mirroring never takes effect. With no mirror, ModelBox quad0 is the +x face and takes texture u 19..28 (u+dz+dx), v 10..20. Quad1 is the -x face and takes u 9..18. In the texture, scaled 2x, the blue ONE plus up arrow face is at px u 38..56 (quad0, model +x). The grey back is at u 18..36 (quad1, model -x). I dumped the pixels and viewed a crop: it reads 'ONE' with an up arrow.

Transform of model +x: Ry(n) followed by Rx(180), which maps (x,y,z) to (x,-y,-z). Meta 2 (n=0) gives +x = E. Meta 3 (n=90): (1,0,0) becomes (0,0,-1) and then (0,0,+1) = S. Meta 4 (n=180) gives W. Meta 5 (n=270) gives N. This agrees with the propgeom box at meta 3: z 0.47..0.56, so the plate is south of the pole centre (pole z 0.469..0.531, plate 0.5..0.5625). It also agrees with propgeom's 'front' column, E S W N.

It also follows the facing-the-placer rule. A placer looking south (yaw 0) stands north of the block and gets meta 5, front N, toward them.

Reader A is wrong. It put the printed face on model -x, which would only be true if mirror were applied (mirror would swap the +x and -x faces). Here mirror is set after addBox and does nothing, so A's W N E S is reversed by 180 degrees. Reader B's E S W N is correct.

I could not check B's claim that the 'USA coast builder used 5 at meta 3 facing the road', so I did not use it. There is NO gallery photo of this block: docs/shots/gallery_v0.16/views.txt lists only the Russian road signs. The result therefore rests on code plus texture, not a photo. I also extracted roadsign_oneway.png as a cross check: it is a red DO NOT ENTER (white bar) on the same face region, so the pairing advice is confirmed. Long axis, x at 3/5 and z at 2/4, comes from prop_geometry.tsv lines 354..357.

judged.name: BlockRoadsignStop
judged.looks_like: A thin grey post about 2 blocks tall with a square red STOP plate (9 px wide, 10 px tall, 1 px thick) on top. The back of the plate is plain grey. A floating "view" world icon is drawn about 2.75 blocks above it.

judged.meta_range_note: Only 2..5 are valid; onBlockPlacedBy sets nothing else. The renderer uses meta % 4 (0 gives 180 degrees, 1 gives 270, 2 gives 0, 3 gives 90). Metadata 0, 1 and 6..15 would still draw, aliasing 4, 5, 2 and 3, but they are not placement values.
real_world_city_use: Each approach of an unsignalised crossing of minor or residential streets (two way or four way stop).
Where an alley, a parking lot exit or a side street joins a main road.
Abandoned city: the same spots, sometimes knocked over or missing. Never at a crossing that has traffic lights.
placement_rules: Right hand traffic. Put it on the right corner of the near side of each approach, on the sidewalk cell next to the curb, about 1 cell before the crosswalk or stop line. The STOP face points toward the drivers coming in.
Northbound approach (traffic moving toward -z): SE corner, face S, meta 3.
Southbound approach (+z): NW corner, face N, meta 5.
Eastbound approach (+x): SW corner, face W, meta 4.
Westbound approach (-x): NE corner, face E, meta 2.
Rule of thumb: the face points back down the approaching lane, which is the same as facing a player standing where the drivers come from (onBlockPlacedBy faces the placer).
Not at crossings with traffic lights. Use at most one per approach.

Keep the 2 cells above it free. The model is drawn up to y + 2.19, and the collision box is 0.4..0.65 by 2.0 high. It is only 0.09 thick, so it can sit in the curb side sidewalk cell without blocking the walkway.
A turned sign shows only its grey back to the drivers, so always check the face direction in a screenshot before signing off.
judged.evidence:
Reader B is right and Reader A is wrong. I worked this out from the code, the vanilla source and the texture. There is no gallery photo to check against: BlockRoadsignStop is not in docs/shots/gallery_v0.16/views.txt, and docs/shots_index.md has no stop sign shot.

(1) Turning. deobf/src/decimation/render/RoadsignStopRenderer.java translates by +0.5, 0, +0.5, then glRotatef(180, 0.1, 0, 0) (180 degrees about x), then glRotatef(n, 0, 1, 0) with n = {meta%4: 0 gives 180, 1 gives 270, 2 gives 0, 3 gives 90}, then ModelRoadsign. Working the model +x normal through Ry(n) and then Rx(180):
- meta 2 (n = 0): +x, East.
- meta 3 (n = 90): +z, South.
- meta 4 (n = 180): -x, West.
- meta 5 (n = 270): -z, North.
propgeom.py show BlockRoadsignStop agrees: the plate is thin in z at meta 3 (box 0.22..0.78 by 0.47..0.56) and its front column reads E/S/W/N.

(2) Which face carries STOP. In ModelRoadsign (deci/p/al), the plate ny is new ModelRenderer(this, 9, 1).addBox(0, 0, 0, 1, 10, 9). Vanilla ModelBox (dev/build/rfg/minecraft-src/.../ModelBox.java) gives quadList[0], the +x face (built on f4 = x + dx), the UV u+dz+dx .. u+2dz+dx, which is columns 19..28, rows 10..20 at 32x64 scale. quadList[1], the -x face, gets columns 9..18. I dumped roadsign_stop.png from the jar (64x128 scaled to 32x64): columns 19..27, rows 10..19 hold the red plate with white letters, and columns 9..18 are plain grey. So STOP is on +x.

(3) Why Reader A went wrong. Reader A assumed the mirror flag swaps the plate to -x. But javap of deci/p/al.class shows `mirror = true` is set AFTER addBox() for both parts. ModelBox reads renderer.mirror only in its constructor, and vanilla ModelRenderer.addBox builds the ModelBox right away. So the mirror flag does nothing here. The usual Techne export pattern holds: STOP stays on +x, and Reader A's whole W/N/E/S table is turned by 180 degrees.

(4) Cross check. BlockRoadsignStop.onBlockPlacedBy maps yaw quadrant 0 (player facing S) to meta 5, 1 (facing W) to 2, 2 (facing N) to 3, and 3 (facing E) to 4. Under the E/S/W/N table every one of these points STOP back at the placer, which is the usual BlockProp rule (docs/prop_placement.md). Under Reader A's table the placer would see only the grey back.

Other facts: the block is a BlockContainer with a TileEntitySpecialRenderer (EntityRoadsignStop, ClientRenderRegistry), and it is not in the loot table. Reader B's placement table (northbound SE m3, southbound NW m5, eastbound SW m4, westbound NE m2) matches the derivation above.

real_world_city_use: Road works and collapsed road or sinkhole sections, standing at the edge of the dig
Police or military checkpoints and quarantine lanes, lighting the inspection area
Crash or pile up scenes on a street or highway, lighting the wrecks

placement_rules: Pick the meta by the DIAGONAL you want to light. Area to the SE of the light: meta 2. SW: meta 3. NW: meta 4. NE: meta 5. Put the light at the outer corner of the area so its diagonal points into the middle.

Stand it on the ground, sidewalk or road shoulder, about 1 cell from the curb or barrier and outside driving lanes, unless it is part of a roadblock.
Drawn 1 x 1 x 2.44: needs 2 free cells above. No fences, nets, awnings, slabs or leaves over it.
Pair it with a power generator 1 to 2 cells away, on the side away from the lit area.

judged.looks_like: Red portable generator in a black open tube frame, filling one whole cell and about 0.875 high. The red body sits low across the -x half with the fuel tank and filler cap on top of it. The engine block and the round pull starter are at the +x end. A small grey control and outlet plate (5x4 px plus 2x2 px) sits on the +z long side. It puffs large smoke and smoke from the top centre all the time, plays an engine loop, and a right click with a battery charges the battery.
judged.front_feature: The control and outlet panel, parts nX (x -6.5..-1.5, y 2.5..6.5 px, z 6.5..7.5) and nW (x -1..1, z 6.5..7.5), on the model's +z face. This is the side a person serves (switch, sockets). It is NOT the side the default placer rule turns toward the placer: that side is the model -x end, which shows the red body and frame. The pull starter or engine end is model +x.
judged.meta_range_note: PropRenderer, yaw metadata % 4 * 90, no extra rotation, no scale. Use 2..5 (0 and 1 repeat 2 and 3 visually). The panel faces 2 S, 3 W, 4 N, 5 E, which is 90 degrees clockwise of the default rule, the same exception as BlockMilitaryRadio. The red body end (the side toward the placer, default rule) faces 2 E, 3 S, 4 W, 5 N. The pull starter or engine end faces 2 W, 3 N, 4 E, 5 S. The panel-less back (model -z) faces 2 N, 3 E, 4 S, 5 W. The drawn box is the full cell at every meta, so facing is only visible up close.
real_world_city_use: Survivor camp, city refuge yard or FOB: next to the tents, clinic, canteen or light tower it powers, against a sandbag ring or wall
Checkpoint, roadblock or crash scene beside a work light or hazard lamp
Field hospital or evacuation centre yard, construction or road works site
Rooftop holdout on the open roof slab
Behind a shop, bar or clinic in the alley as backup power, only where survivors still live. A running, smoking generator says somebody is here.
placement_rules: Outdoors or under an open-sided shed only. It smokes at y+1.02 every display tick, so keep the cell above free and never put it under a ceiling. Real-world CO guidance puts generators about 6 m from doors and windows. In game use at least 3 cells from any door or window of a lived-in room.

Point the panel toward the walkway or the person who serves it. Walkway SOUTH: meta 2. WEST: meta 3. NORTH: meta 4. EAST: meta 5. Do not use the default propFacing rule for this prop: it would turn the red body end, not the panel, toward the path.
The back (model -z, no panel) goes against the wall or sandbag ring. Back to the north wall: meta 2. East wall: 3. South wall: 4. West wall: 5.
Leave the panel side cell free so a player can step up and right click it (battery charging).
Use it only in inhabited sites (camps, refuges, military, checkpoints), because it runs forever (smoke plus the engine sound). In a dead city block it reads wrong.
Pair it with what it powers (a work light tower, BlockHazardLight or BlockHazardLamp 1 to 3 cells away) and with fuel (barrels or drums 1 to 2 cells away, not touching the engine end).
At most 1 per camp corner or scene, and at most 2 side by side in a base generator yard.
Drawn exactly 1 x 1 x 0.875 with no overhang. The collision box is 1 x 0.8 x 1.
